newsitem.title: UK: Middle East, West Africa crude tankers steady.
newsitem.headline: Middle East, West Africa crude tankers steady.

text.p: Middle East crude tanker rates were steady on Thursday, while West Africa-U.S. routes were also little changed, defying earlier predictions of a sharply higher market, brokers said.
Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) on Middle East-West routes stayed at around W55, while to Japan they were pegged at around W62.5 for modern vessels and in the mid-50s older ships.

In the West African sector, some brokers were less bullish than on Wednesday, when they forecast rates of over W90 for 130,000 tonne ships. They said the rate on Thursday remained at about W85, with VLCCs still at around W60.

"There's a lot of activity in West Africa. It may go very slightly up but we don't see an enormous increase," said a Norwegian broker. "There is not yet a shortage of ships and we see a great one coming."
In the Mediterranean, an Italian broker said, "Activity is quite strong, especially Suezmaxes." He reported Suezmax fixtures at W85-90, against W82.5 on Wednesday.
"There are also signs that Aframaxes may pick up. There is a lack of prompt tonnage and good quality ships. We may see better numbers next week," the broker added.
Cross-Med Aframaxes were fixed around W105, unchanged .
Transatlantic fixtures featured a number of smaller vessels with few of the more usual VLCCs due to size restrictions at many Canadian and U.S. east coast ports, they added.
Typical was the Canadian Liberty carrying 80,000 tonnes from Sullom Voe to Halifax at W145 for Exxon, they said.
Caribs-U.S. Gulf 70,000 tonners were steady at W162.5 as weather worries abated early in the day, although two Mexican ports later closed due to storms.
